title: mosaic-auth-tiling-and-checkpointed-streams-cross-sdk-ergonomic-bump
author: Aisha Raman
description: Introduce 'mosaic auth tiling' (credential tiling) and checkpointed streaming across Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs. Motivation: high-concurrency streaming customers observed token-rotation contention and non-deterministic retry amplification when many streams concurrently triggered credential refresh. Mosaic auth tiling shards credential refresh responsibilities by request fingerprint to avoid global locks while preserving fallback semantics. Checkpointed streaming adds an opt-in resume token to streaming client surfaces so long-lived reads can be resumed idempotently after network failures or client restarts. This PR implements the runtime primitives, surface ergonomics changes, tests, example updates and coordinated version bumps. Checklist: - [x] core credential tiler implementation (py/ts/go) - [x] checkpoint/resume API on streaming clients (AsyncCheckpointIterator / StreamClient.checkpoint / StreamCheckpoint interface) - [x] feature gate and runtime flagging (enable_mosaic_auth default: false) - [x] unit + flaky-resiliency integration tests - [x] docs, examples and migration guide - [x] bump package versions for release Notes: Gate the new behavior behind a flag so we can stage rollout; older clients are unaffected. Migration notes included in docs_impacted and release_notes. Linked items: ENG-1420 ENG-1435

release_notes:
- Introduced credential tiling (mosaic auth) to reduce refresh contention under high concurrency.
- Added opt-in checkpointed streaming API to allow idempotent resume of long-lived streams.
- Python SDK: AsyncCheckpointIterator and session credential_tiler available behind flag.
- TypeScript SDK: StreamClient.checkpoint() and iterator ergonomics.
- Go SDK: StreamCheckpoint interface and helpers.
Note: features are feature-gated (enable_mosaic_auth=false by default).
